findings.title: Hindquarters are a closed box: no flank or stifle fold, no split between the thighs, no 'second thigh' line to the hock
findings.observed: The TRUNK rings behind the hip joint are full-width closed loops with a flat floor: x=-0.52 is 0.50 m wide and 0.76 m deep with its bottom at 0.845, and x=-0.68 is 0.47 wide and 0.74 deep with its bottom at 0.85. Their girth (1.95 m perimeter at -0.52) equals the heart girth. The caudal outline runs from the buttock cap (-0.91, 1.27) down and forward to the trunk's bottom-rear corner (-0.68, 0.85), then jumps to the gaskin's back surface at about (-0.57, 0.83), before going back again to the point of hock (-0.70, 0.57). That is a 30 cm forward undercut. In 00-stand 'hindleg, right side' the rump ends in a horizontal shelf with the gaskin sprouting out from under it. In 'stand: rear' the quarters are one block with a flat bottom edge and the legs come out of its underside.
findings.expected: In profile the TB's caudal thigh line (semitendinosus and semimembranosus, the 'second thigh') drops almost vertically from the point of buttock, then runs down the gaskin and calcaneal tendon to the point of hock, which lies close to the buttock plumb line. In front of the stifle the flank fold rises from the stifle to the belly. From behind, the thighs are separate rounded masses that part below the perineum in an inverted U well above the hocks, and the widest point is at the stifles.
findings.evidence: index.html:491-495 TRUNK rows -0.86..-0.52 (bottoms 1.13, 0.99, 0.85, 0.845); index.html:396 PROF.trunk (closed profile, no ventral notch); index.html:1185-1187 femur (inward 0.02, back depth 0.18-0.22) and tibia meshes; tiles 00-stand 'stand: hindleg, right side', 'stand: rear', 'stand: 3/4 rear-left'

fixOptions.label: Let the limbs carry the lower quarters
fixOptions.approach: Raise the floor of the TRUNK rows at x <= -0.36 to about 0.98-1.05 (flank and perineum level). Deepen the femur mesh's caudal sections (t 0.5-1.08) so the thigh itself forms the outline from the buttock down to the gaskin.
fixOptions.risk: Trunk and thigh are on different bones, so seams or gaps can open in hip flexion/extension at the gallop. Shading discontinuities appear where the meshes meet.

fixOptions.label: Add a skinned buttock/second-thigh mass
fixOptions.approach: Add a mass per side running from the tuber ischii to the gaskin, weighted to hips and femur (like the triceps blob on the arm).
fixOptions.risk: mergeRigid gives rigid parts single-bone weights, so a two-bone blend needs new skinning code. It may stretch at full extension.

fixOptions.label: Notch the rear rings
fixOptions.approach: Use a rump profile variant for rings at x < -0.6 with a ventral midline groove, so the rear view shows two thighs and a perineal split.
fixOptions.risk: Low. The profile only affects the rear rings (the saddle reads rows in front of about x=-0.4).

references: Budras KD, Sack WO, Röck S, Anatomy of the Horse, 6th ed. (surface anatomy of the hindquarter: semitendinosus/semimembranosus, flank fold, stifle)
Baxter GM (ed.), Adams and Stashak's Lameness in Horses, 6th ed., 2011, ch. 2 (rear view: plumb line from the tuber ischii bisecting the limb; caudal profile to the point of hock)

findings.title: Croup cross-section is a narrow peaked ridge with no points of hip: the rear view reads 'rafter-hipped' and pear-shaped
findings.observed: At the croup peak (TRUNK x=-0.52: w 0.25, wu 0.8) the PROF.trunk profile gives a half-width of 0.107 m just 3.8 cm below the top and only about 0.146 m (29 cm across) 10 cm below the top. Below that the sides fall at about 58 deg to the widest point at mid-depth. No tuber coxae (point of hip) prominence exists anywhere. In 00-stand 'stand: rear' (zoomed) the croup forms an A-frame apex, and the quarters widen like a bell to their maximum at about gaskin-top height.
findings.expected: A fit TB's croup is broad and rounded over the sacrum. The tubera coxae form the 'corners' of the hindquarters about 10-15 cm below the croup top, roughly as wide as or wider than the chest (TB chest width 43.8 cm, Ünal 2025), with the quarters widest at the stifles. From the side the point of hip is a visible landmark above the stifle and in front of the croup peak.
findings.evidence: index.html:396 PROF.trunk [[0,1],[0.52,0.9],[0.9,0.5],...]; index.html:493-496 TRUNK rows -0.68..-0.36 (wu 0.78-0.82); tiles 00-stand 'stand: rear', 'stand: 3/4 rear-left', 'stand: top'

fixOptions.label: Flatten the rump top
fixOptions.approach: Raise wu to about 0.95-1.05 for the TRUNK rows at x -0.68..-0.36, and/or use a rump profile with a flatter top (for example [0.7, 0.92] instead of [0.52, 0.9]).
fixOptions.risk: Low. It reduces the low-poly 'facet' read slightly. The tail groove and saddle are unaffected.

fixOptions.label: Add tuber coxae
fixOptions.approach: Add two small bony prominences (extra ring vertices or a small skinned wedge on the hips bone) at about x -0.42, z +/-0.23, y 1.46.
fixOptions.risk: Must ride on the hips bone without popping during lumbosacral flexion (BODY.race).

fixOptions.label: Muscled-rump profile
fixOptions.approach: Use a dedicated profile with a shallow midline gutter between rounded gluteal masses, typical of fit racehorses.
fixOptions.risk: More vertices. The tail root must be re-seated in the gutter.

references: Ünal N et al. (2025) Arch Anim Breed 68:253 (TB chest width 43.79 cm, front chest width 21.77 cm)
Matsuura A et al. (2021) J Equine Sci 32:73-79, doi:10.1294/jes.32.73 (hip/waist width defined between the tubera coxae, croup width between the hip joints)
Budras KD et al., Anatomy of the Horse, 6th ed. (tuber coxae / tuber sacrale surface landmarks)

findings.title: Scapula as short as the humerus (1:1); its top ends 12 cm below the withers, so the shoulder is short and the arm long
findings.observed: Scapula (FORE.sc to FORE.sh) is 0.356 m at 51.4 deg; humerus is 0.354 m at 47.7 deg; humerus/scapula is 0.99. The scapula top (0.498, 1.50) is 0.122 m below and 0.041 m in front of the withers. The 'shoulder' measured from withers to point of shoulder (about 0.80, 1.22) is 0.53 m, giving arm/shoulder 0.67 and forearm/shoulder 0.87. The shoulder joint is 1.222 m high (75.3% of WH). The joint angles are TB-like (shoulder joint 99 deg, elbow 138 deg); the lengths are off.
findings.expected: Jumping TBs: shoulder 69 cm, arm 34 cm, forearm 46 cm, giving arm/shoulder 49.7% and forearm/shoulder 66.6% (Senna et al. 2015). The model's arm (0.354) and forearm (0.460) match these, but its shoulder is about 25% short. Anatomically the scapula with its cartilage is about 1.4-1.5 times the joint-to-joint humerus, and its dorsal border reaches up close to the withers. TB point-of-shoulder height is about 113.7 cm at 157.9 cm withers (72%), about 1.17 m at 163 cm.
findings.evidence: index.html:536 FORE {sc:[0.5,1.5], sh:[0.72,1.22], el:[0.48,0.96]}; index.html:1164 scapula mesh; index.html:1168 arm mesh; index.html:1176-1177 L.rest/L.len feed the IK; index.html:1394 ARM_RANGE; measurements static.standing RF scapTop/shoulder/elbow; tile 00-stand 'stand: right side', 'stand: foreleg, right side'

fixOptions.label: Lengthen the scapula and shorten the humerus
fixOptions.approach: Raise FORE.sc to about (0.44-0.46, 1.58) and lower the shoulder joint to about (0.70, 1.18), keeping the 99 deg and 138 deg joint angles, so scapula is about 0.42-0.44 and humerus about 0.30.
fixOptions.risk: L.len.arm changes the forelimb IK reach and ARM_RANGE behaviour in the swing. The blade top would protrude more unless the shoulder-fin issue is fixed together. Chest rows near the point of shoulder may need re-fitting.

fixOptions.label: Extend only the visible blade
fixOptions.approach: Start the scapula mesh at t of about -0.25 so the shoulder line reaches the withers. The joints are unchanged.
fixOptions.risk: The longer lever exaggerates the scapular swing (scapSwing up to 18 deg in the race) at the top. Clipping with the neck root and mane.

fixOptions.label: Lower the point of shoulder only
fixOptions.approach: Move FORE.sh down about 4-5 cm along the humerus and re-fit the TRUNK front rows (x 0.68-0.81).
fixOptions.risk: Small. It slightly shortens the arm and changes the breast silhouette.

references: Senna NA et al. (2015) Asian J Anim Sci 9:208-216 (shoulder 69 +/- 5, arm 34 +/- 2.9, forearm 46 +/- 2.4, fore cannon 28.67 cm; shoulder joint 99 deg, elbow 138.4 deg)
Ünal N et al. (2025) Arch Anim Breed 68:253 (TB shoulder height 113.67 cm at withers 157.92 cm)
Ahmad I et al. (2025) Evaluating forelimb and hindlimb joint conformation of Morna racehorses. Vet Sci 12:20, doi:10.3390/vetsci12010020 (shoulder vs ground 58.4 deg; review of TB values)

findings.title: Withers not defined: the topline rises steadily from the back into the neck, with the crest rooted behind the withers peak
findings.observed: Topline heights: 1.53 at x=0, 1.545 at 0.18, 1.595 at 0.34 and 1.625 at 0.46 (the 'withers' landmark at 1.622 sits here). The neck crest starts at (0.40, 1.63), 6 cm behind the withers peak, and climbs to 1.73 at x of about 0.60. There is no local high point or change of slope where back meets neck, so the 'withers' is just a point on a rising line. In 00-stand 'left side' and 'right side' the back flows straight up into the crest.
findings.expected: TBs are known for high, well-defined withers that extend well back. The tall spinous processes of about T3-T9 (highest about T4-T6) form a distinct ridge between the end of the mane and the saddle area. The crest meets the withers in front of their summit, and the withers summit sets the withers height.
findings.evidence: index.html:497-504 TRUNK top values x 0..0.46; index.html:512 NECK row 0 crest (0.4, 1.63); index.html:664-665 neck stretch about NB (0.55, 1.4); measurements static.standing withers; tiles 00-stand 'stand: left side', 'stand: right side'

fixOptions.label: Re-seat the crest root and peak the withers
fixOptions.approach: Move NECK row 0's crest point forward and down (about (0.50, 1.60)) and raise the TRUNK tops at x 0.34-0.46 by 2-4 cm, so a short dip in front of the withers marks the junction.
fixOptions.risk: Withers height (the 163 cm reference used for scaling) changes slightly, as do the front edge of the saddle cloth and mane-blade roots.

fixOptions.label: Add a withers ridge
fixOptions.approach: Add a narrow skinned wedge along x 0.15-0.50 on top of the trunk (chest/spine weighted) that extends the withers back under the saddle.
fixOptions.risk: Low. It may poke through the saddle cloth unless the drape grows a little there.

references: Budras KD et al., Anatomy of the Horse, 6th ed. (withers formed by the spinous processes of the cranial thoracic vertebrae)
Baxter GM (ed.), Adams and Stashak's Lameness in Horses, 6th ed., 2011, ch. 2 (withers description in conformation evaluation)

findings.title: Barrel too big for a 475 kg racing TB, with almost no tuck-up toward the flank
findings.observed: Heart girth (ring perimeter at x=0.34) is 1.95 m, the same as the rings at x=0.18 and x=-0.52. The barrel is 0.56 m wide at x=0-0.18. The Wagner & Tyler formula with a 166-177 cm body length gives about 530-565 kg, against the stated 475 kg. The underline is almost flat: 0.826 at the girth (x=0.18), 0.855 at x=0, 0.89 at -0.19, then back down to 0.845 at -0.52. In 00-stand 'left side' the belly is a level line from the elbow to the stifle.
findings.expected: BW = girth^2 x body length / 11880 (cm). For 475 kg at a 163-166 cm body length the heart girth is about 1.84-1.86 m. A racing-fit TB is lean in the flank: the underline rises from the girth behind the elbow toward the flank and sheath, and the barrel tapers into the loin.
findings.evidence: index.html:496-503 TRUNK rows -0.36..0.34 (w 0.255-0.28, bottoms 0.83-0.89); index.html:700-702 belly/bulk scaling; tile 00-stand 'stand: left side', 'stand: 3/4 front-right'

fixOptions.label: Slim and tuck the barrel
fixOptions.approach: Reduce TRUNK w0 at x -0.36..0.34 by about 5%. Raise the bottoms at x -0.36..0 by 4-6 cm so the line climbs from the girth to the flank.
fixOptions.risk: The saddle girth and cloth drape (rowAt) change shape. The bulk factor for heavy horses starts from a leaner base.

fixOptions.label: Fitness/tuck as a conformation parameter
fixOptions.approach: Add conf.tuck (or tie it to race fitness) to blend the flank bottoms and barrel width, defaulting to a racing-fit tuck.
fixOptions.risk: One more parameter to keep consistent with bulk and the saddle drape.

references: Wagner EL, Tyler PJ (2011) A comparison of weight estimation methods in adult horses. J Equine Vet Sci 31:706-710 (BW = girth^2 x length / 11880), as applied in Matsuura A et al. (2021) J Equine Sci 32:73-79

findings.title: Breast hangs forward of and below the elbow ('pot' in front of the forelegs)
findings.observed: The brisket landmark is at (0.583, 0.898): 10 cm in front of the elbow joint and 6 cm below it. The chest floor at x=0.58/0.68 sits at 0.90/0.95, below the elbow (0.96), and the front of the chest reaches x=0.81 (cap 0.86). That is 23-28 cm in front of the forearm's front edge (about 0.575 at elbow height). In 00-stand 'left side', 'right side' and 'foreleg, right side' a rounded mass bulges in front of the forearm tops, and the forearm enters the body behind it.
findings.expected: In profile the point of shoulder is the most cranial point. Below it the breast (pectoralis descendens) curves back and meets the front of the forearm at about elbow height. The lowest point of the chest is at the girth just behind the elbows, not in front of them.
findings.evidence: index.html:501-508 TRUNK brisket rows x 0.46..0.81 (bottoms 0.87, 0.90, 0.95, 1.02, 1.10) and the comment there; index.html:708 front cap; measurements static.standing brisket vs RF elbow; tiles 00-stand 'stand: foreleg, right side', 'stand: left side'

fixOptions.label: Raise and pull back the breast floor
fixOptions.approach: Raise the TRUNK bottoms at x 0.58/0.68 to about 0.96/1.02 and the front ring and cap back about 3 cm, so the breast meets the forearm at elbow height.
fixOptions.risk: The code comment says the deep floor hides the forearm top. A gap or visible seam may appear in front of the elbow when the humerus swings forward at the gallop or race.

fixOptions.label: Shape the pectorals instead
fixOptions.approach: Keep the depth but narrow wd at x 0.58-0.68 and add a midline groove so the breast reads as two pectoral bulges between the legs rather than a single pot.
fixOptions.risk: Low. Only the front view changes noticeably.

references: Budras KD et al., Anatomy of the Horse, 6th ed. (pectoral muscles; point of shoulder; topography of the sternum relative to the elbow)

findings.title: Fore pastern about 4-5 deg more upright than measured TB values
findings.observed: FORE.pastern is 33 deg from vertical, so the fore pastern stands 57.0 deg to the ground and the fore fetlock joint angle is 147.2 deg. The hind pastern is 60.0 deg (hind fetlock 147.3 deg).
findings.expected: Jumping TBs: fore fetlock 142.7 +/- 6 deg (a pastern of about 52-53 deg to the ground), hind fetlock 149.8 +/- 8 deg (Senna et al. 2015). Clinical guides give a fore hoof-pastern axis of about 50-54 deg, with the hind 2-5 deg steeper. TBs typically show long, sloping fore pasterns.
findings.evidence: index.html:536 FORE.pastern 33*DEG; index.html:537 HIND.pastern 30*DEG; index.html:1157 fetlock from coffin and pastern angle; index.html:1350-1355 plantedFetlock; tile 00-stand 'stand: foreleg, right side'

fixOptions.label: Slope the fore pastern
fixOptions.approach: Set FORE.pastern to about 37-38 deg from vertical. Re-check the hoof wall angle (HOOF_SHAPE / hoofGeo) so the hoof-pastern axis stays unbroken.
fixOptions.risk: Fetlock height drops about 1 cm, which shifts the fore IK target and the stance sag look. The breakover feel changes slightly.

fixOptions.label: Per-horse pastern conformation
fixOptions.approach: Expose conf.pastern (upright to sloping) as part of the requested customisation, defaulting to about 37 deg fore and 32 deg hind.
fixOptions.risk: The hoof shape must follow the parameter or the axis breaks.

references: Senna NA et al. (2015) Asian J Anim Sci 9:208-216 (fore fetlock 142.73 +/- 6 deg, hind fetlock 149.84 +/- 8 deg)
Baxter GM (ed.), Adams and Stashak's Lameness in Horses, 6th ed., 2011, ch. 2 (hoof-pastern axis guidelines)

findings.title: From behind, the hind limbs are perfectly parallel posts: no stifle-out, hock-in, toe-out set
findings.observed: Every hind joint shares one z: hip 0.169, hock 0.173, toe 0.176. The femur mesh is only shifted 2 cm inward. The hind limb is a vertical plane with the toes straight ahead. In 00-stand 'stand: rear' the gaskins, hocks and cannons run as straight parallel columns, 35 cm apart centre to centre (fore 33 cm).
findings.expected: Normal horses carry the hind limb slightly rotated outward: stifles point a little outward to clear the abdomen, hocks sit slightly closer together, and toes turn slightly out (a mild, normal outward rotation, not cow-hocks). The plumb line from the tuber ischii still bisects hock, cannon and hoof.
findings.evidence: index.html:537 HIND.z 0.175; index.html:1151-1152 one z per leg; index.html:1185 femur inward offset; measurements static.standing RH/LH z; tile 00-stand 'stand: rear'

fixOptions.label: Toe-out the lower limb only
fixOptions.approach: Yaw the hind pastern and hoof meshes (or the hoof joint) 5-8 deg outward about the vertical.
fixOptions.risk: Low. Footprints and racing plates rotate with the hoof.

fixOptions.label: Rotate the whole hind limb plane
fixOptions.approach: Apply a small outward yaw of the femur joint so the stifle points out and the hock in, with the IK still solving in that rotated plane.
fixOptions.risk: solveLeg/abductedZ assume a plane parallel to x-y. The stride direction of the hind hooves would need correcting.

references: Baxter GM (ed.), Adams and Stashak's Lameness in Horses, 6th ed., 2011, ch. 2 (rear-view conformation; slight outward rotation of the hind limb)
Ross MW, Dyson SJ (eds), Diagnosis and Management of Lameness in the Horse, 2nd ed., 2011, ch. 4 Conformation and Lameness
